findings.title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author links
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new light branch uses 70%, which changes the existing light-theme color and makes embedded post usernames much fainter. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the light value and uses (100 - x) for the dark one, so this should be (30%, 70%).

findings.title: Light-theme value inverted for .custom-message-length
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new code uses 30% for the light branch, so the hint text becomes noticeably darker on light themes. The desktop version of this rule correctly uses (70%, 30%); the mobile one should match.

findings.title: Topic map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The new code uses 50% for light and 50% for dark, which visibly lightens mobile topic-map headings on light themes. The desktop equivalent correctly uses (20%, 80%), so this should match.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new light branch uses 50%, which changes the existing light-theme appearance. It should be (30%, 70%) to preserve current behavior.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same issue as on desktop: the original rule used 30% lightness, but the light branch is now 50%. This changes the light-theme color and should be (30%, 70%).
